The answer today is yes, by hand: after any merge touching open-brain/src, update the main checkout to master, rebuild, and have every open session run /mcp reconnect open-brain. That is a step that works only while someone remembers it, and it was missed. MEASURED 2026-09-22: the main tree was at 0bf0597, 24 commits behind origin/master 9788064, while every check read green, because build-freshness compares the main tree's build to the main tree's own HEAD and never to master (G-034). The SessionStart hook prints a tree-currency line for the seat's own checkout but none for the checkout actually serving the hooks and the MCP server. FIX SHAPE, deterministic first: (1) cli-bootstrap prints, first, 'serving build: <sha>, N behind origin/master (last fetch <time>)' for the MAIN tree, however the session was launched; it reads refs locally and never fetches; (2) one command, e.g. `open-brain main-tree update`, which refuses on a dirty tree or on commits not on origin/master (the detach command's three refusals), fast-forwards, rebuilds, and reads build-freshness back against origin/master rather than trusting exit codes. It then says which sessions must reconnect, because only the human can. The reconnect cannot be automated from inside a session. Relates to G-033, G-034, T-154. — FINDING, planner session 150 (from T-201's stop): StateSchema is z.strictObject at every level, so ANY new field written to master's record blinds every checkout whose build predates it, including the main tree that serves every session's MCP server. - [x] **T-279** Read the Win32 process table through an ASCII-safe pipe, and correct T-270's comment and test docstring: the C0 bytes come from the console's cp437 best-fit encoding, not ConvertTo-Json (session 171) — s170 root cause (see T-270's note): Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes its stdout in the console OEM code page 437 with .NET best-fit, so → • § ¶ ← ↑ ↓ ↔ ☺ ► arrive as C0 bytes, and non-ASCII without a cp437 glyph arrives as U+FFFD (· and ✓ seen live). T-270 makes the parse survive by turning C0 into spaces, but command lines are still read lossily. Fix shape to weigh: escape every non-ASCII character to \uXXXX inside PowerShell before it writes (a regex replace on ConvertTo-Json's output; 5.1 has no -EscapeHandling), so the pipe carries ASCII only; or set [Console]::OutputEncoding to UTF-8 (it can throw with no console). Keep T-270's replacement as defence in depth. Correct process-session.ts's T-270 comment and the t270 test file's docstring. ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED, first-hand on the desktop: ConvertTo-Json escapes control characters (\u001a) on BOTH PCs (PS 5.1.19041.6456, CLR 4.0.30319.42000). The raw C0 bytes are made on the PowerShell-to-Node pipe by the console's OEM cp437 best-fit encoder: → 0x1A, ← 0x1B, ↑ 0x18, ↓ 0x19, ↔ 0x1D, • 0x07, § 0x15, ¶ 0x14, ☺ 0x01, ► 0x10 (other non-ASCII: U+FFFD or a best-fit ASCII). So any process whose command line held an arrow or a bullet broke the table on every Windows host, and the brief's raw-0x1A sleeper could never reproduce (the brief now carries a Correction section).
